mainTopic: The meaning of 'שבועה שאוכל' in two משניות, and the מחלוקת of אביי and רבא about מבטא, איסר and מתפיס בשבועה
overview: The גמרא finishes resolving a contradiction about the oath 'שבועה שאוכל'. Our משנה reads it as 'I will eat,' but the משנה in נדרים reads it as 'I will not eat of yours.' The first answer is that in נדרים people were pressing him to eat, so his words mean 'I won't eat.' רב אשי instead reads the words in נדרים as 'שאי אוכל'. That case is listed to teach that we don't call it a slip of the tongue. Next comes a ברייתא saying that the words מבטא and איסר mean a שבועה, though its wording seems to contradict itself. אביי explains that איסר means attaching to an existing שבועה, and the גמרא tests his sources from the פסוקים. רבא explains instead that איסר is a middle word, which becomes a נדר or a שבועה depending on the wording used. The גמרא shows that each view fits their known מחלוקת about מתפיס בשבועה. It then brings a ברייתא and a comment of שמואל about איסר as attaching to a vow, which fits אביי, and begins a challenge against רבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Context explains the oath: were they pressing him to eat?
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה speaks of a man nobody is pressing to eat, so 'שבועה שאוכל' means he will eat. The משנה in נדרים speaks of a man being pressed to eat, so his oath means he will not eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...pressing him to eat. Our משנה is a case where they are not pressing him to eat. The outside משנה is a case where they are pressing him to eat, and he keeps saying 'I won't eat, I won't eat.' So when he swears, this is what he means: 'I swear I will not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer to the contradiction between the two משניות. The situation shows what the man meant by his words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words, 'שבועה שאוכל', can mean opposite things depending on the setting. If friends are begging him to eat and he keeps refusing, his oath obviously continues his refusal. With no such pressure, the words keep their plain meaning: 'I will eat.'

keyTerms.meaning: They are pressing or urging him
Our משנה (here in שבועות)
Here it means the 'outside' משנה, in נדרים
I will not eat
He swears, takes an oath

steps.confusionAlert: Here the word בָּרַיְיתָא does not mean a normal ברייתא. It means the משנה in מסכת נדרים, which is 'outside' our מסכת.

phrases.english: ...pressing him to eat.
Our משנה is where they are not pressing him to eat;
the outside משנה is where they are pressing him to eat,
and he is saying 'I won't eat' and 'I won't eat,'
so when he swears, this is what he is saying:
'I swear that I will not eat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the contradiction between the משנה in שבועות and the משנה in נדרים raised earlier on the דף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each משנה speaks of a different situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two משניות read the same words in opposite ways, so they seem to contradict.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה has no pressure to eat, so the words keep their plain meaning. The משנה in נדרים has pressure to eat, so the words mean 'I will not eat.'

steps.title: רב אשי changes the wording in נדרים
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers differently: read the משנה in נדרים as 'שבועה שאי אוכל לך', which plainly means 'I won't eat of yours.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Teach it as 'I swear that I will not (שאי) eat of yours.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a second way to solve the contradiction. He fixes the wording of the משנה in נדרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the setting, רב אשי says the words themselves are different. 'שאי אוכל' is a way of saying 'I will not eat,' so there is no clash with our משנה, where 'שאוכל' means 'I will eat.'

keyTerms.meaning: That I will not eat

phrases.english: רב אשי said:
Teach: 'I swear that I will not eat of yours.'
phrases.notes: He changes 'שאוכל' in the משנה in נדרים to 'שאי אוכל', so it plainly means 'I won't eat.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the same contradiction answered in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in נדרים seems to use 'שאוכל' to mean 'I won't eat.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The correct wording is 'שאי אוכל', which means 'I won't eat,' so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: Why say the same oath twice?
steps.stepSummary: If the first oath in נדרים is 'שאי אוכל לך', it means the same as the next oath, 'שלא אוכל לך'. So why does the משנה list it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it need to be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי's reading. Now the משנה seems to repeat itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in נדרים also lists 'שלא אוכל לך'. If 'שאי אוכל לך' means exactly the same thing, the משנה would be saying the same rule twice, and a משנה does not normally waste words.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why does it need to be said? What is new here?

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's new reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's reading 'שבועה שאי אוכל לך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With that reading, the משנה lists two oaths that mean the same thing, which seems pointless.

steps.title: It teaches that we don't call it a slip of the tongue
steps.stepSummary: The משנה needs this case so we don't think the unusual wording was a slip of the tongue. It teaches that the oath counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: his tongue slipped. So it teaches us that it is not so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 3. The extra case is there to teach something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שאי אוכל' sounds a lot like 'שאוכל' ('I will eat'). We might think he meant to swear that he would eat and his tongue slipped. The משנה teaches that we don't assume that; his words mean 'I won't eat' and the oath counts.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, you might have thought
His tongue, his words
Stumbled, slipped
It teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the contradiction. (1) The setting decides: being pressed to eat makes 'שאוכל' mean 'I won't eat.' (2) רב אשי: the wording in נדרים is 'שאי אוכל', and it is listed to teach that we don't call it a slip of the tongue.

phrases.english: You might have said:
his tongue slipped on him,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected spelling. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and defends רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a new point (חידוש) that justifies the extra case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Saying 'שאי אוכל' might be a slip of the tongue for 'שאוכל', so the oath would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: We don't assume a slip of the tongue; the oath 'I won't eat' counts.

steps.title: ברייתא: מבטא and איסר are words of oath
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the words מבטא and איסר from the פסוקים in נדרים mean a שבועה. It then says: 'If you say איסר is a שבועה, he is חייב; if not, he is פטור.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'מבטא' means an oath. 'איסר' means an oath. About the prohibition 'איסר': if you say 'איסר' is an oath, he is חייב; if not, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about words that count as an oath. Its last line sounds unsure, and that sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים in פרשת נדרים use the words מבטא and איסר, and the ברייתא says both mean a שבועה. But the ברייתא then speaks as if it is unsure whether איסר is a שבועה ('if you say...'). That seems to clash with what it just said.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear saying of the lips, from the פסוק
A bond, a binding prohibition
Liable (punishable)
Exempt (not punishable)

phrases.english: The רבנן taught:
'Utterance' means an oath.
'Bond' means an oath.
As for the prohibition of 'bond':
if you say 'bond' is an oath, he is liable;
and if not, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the contradiction just resolved.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מבטא and איסר are words of שבועה. Someone who uses איסר is חייב if איסר counts as a שבועה, and פטור if it does not.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to contradict itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: how can the ברייתא say 'if you say איסר is a שבועה' when it already said plainly that איסר is a שבועה?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If you say איסר is an oath'?! But you just said that איסר is an oath!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא seems to contradict itself. The answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The start of the ברייתא states for sure that איסר is a שבועה. The end speaks as if this is uncertain. The גמרא will now need to explain what the ending really means.

keyTerms.meaning: But you (already) said

phrases.english: 'If you say bond is an oath'?!
But you said: bond is an oath!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The last line of the ברייתא: 'אם אתה אומר איסר שבועה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא already stated for sure that איסר is a שבועה, so it cannot then treat this as uncertain.

steps.title: אביי explains what the ברייתא really means
steps.stepSummary: אביי says מבטא is a real שבועה, and איסר is attaching something to an existing שבועה. The ברייתא's 'if you say' is about whether attaching counts like saying a שבועה yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is what the ברייתא means. 'מבטא' is a שבועה. 'איסר' is attaching to a שבועה. As for the איסור of איסר: if you hold that attaching to a שבועה is like saying a שבועה with your own mouth, he is חייב. If not, he is פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 6 by giving איסר a different meaning than מבטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, it sounded like the ברייתא said איסר is a שבועה and then doubted it. אביי explains that the two words mean different things. מבטא is a plain שבועה, and איסר means linking a new item to something already forbidden by a שבועה. The open question ('if you say') is only whether that linking works like a full שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא is explaining the true meaning of a text)
Attaching something to an existing שבועה, for example 'this should be forbidden just like that'
Like saying a שבועה out loud with his own mouth
Liable / exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think אביי says איסר has nothing to do with שבועה. It is still in the world of שבועה. It is just a linked form, and the ברייתא doubts whether that linked form fully counts.

phrases.english: Abaye said: This is what it is saying:
"Mivta" means an oath.
"Issar" means attaching to an oath.
phrases.notes: Picture someone saying 'this food is forbidden to me just like that food,' where the other food was already forbidden by a שבועה.

phrases.english: As for the prohibition of issar:
if you say that attaching to an oath
is like saying an oath with his own mouth, he is liable;
and if not, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא said איסר is a שבועה and then oddly doubted it
steps.terutzMaskana: איסר means attaching to a שבועה. The doubt is whether attaching equals saying a שבועה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that מבטא is a שבועה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins checking אביי's explanation by asking for the source that מבטא means a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that מבטא is a שבועה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing אביי's explanation by asking for a source. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי gave the two words different meanings. Now the גמרא wants each meaning backed by a פסוק, starting with מבטא.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where do we know that mivta is an oath?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines אביי's explanation
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that מבטא means a שבועה

steps.title: The פסוק links מבטא to swearing
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק 'או נפש כי תשבע לבטא בשפתים', which joins לבטא with swearing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Or if a person swears, לבטא with the lips.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that uses the word לבטא in a sentence about swearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'תשבע' (swears) right next to 'לבטא', so מבטא describes the act of swearing itself.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)
To say clearly with the lips

phrases.english: as it is written: "Or if a person swears,
to clearly utter with the lips"

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״אוֹ נֶפֶשׁ כִּי תִשָּׁבַע לְבַטֵּא בִשְׂפָתַיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק joins לבטא to תשבע, so מבטא is a שבועה

steps.title: But איסר is also called a שבועה in a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that איסר also appears as a שבועה, in 'כל נדר וכל שבועת איסר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: איסר also seems to be a שבועה, as it is written: 'Every נדר and every שבועת איסר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי: a פסוק seems to call איסר a שבועה too, just like מבטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a פסוק linking a word to swearing proves that it means a שבועה, then 'שבועת איסר' should prove that איסר also means a plain שבועה. That would erase אביי's difference between the two words.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
An oath of איסר, a binding oath

phrases.english: Issar too is an oath,
as it is written: "Every vow and every oath of issar"

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיסָּר נָמֵי – דִּכְתִיב: ״כׇּל נֵדֶר וְכׇל שְׁבֻעַת אִסָּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same kind of proof as step 9 to attack אביי
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that איסר is only attaching, not a plain שבועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: איסר is joined to 'שבועה' in a פסוק just as מבטא is, so it should also mean a plain שבועה

steps.title: The real question: where do we learn איסר means attaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its question. The real need is a source showing that איסר means attaching to a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, from where do we know that איסר means attaching to a שבועה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that both words are linked to שבועה. It now asks for the source of the new idea in אביי's explanation: איסר as attaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' shows the גמרא is dropping the first question. The question is no longer why מבטא is a שבועה. It is what shows that איסר is the special linked kind.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the earlier approach and asks it a new way)

phrases.english: Rather, from where do we know
that issar is attaching to an oath?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִמַּאי דְּאִיסָּר מִיתְּפֵס בִּשְׁבוּעָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the question after the challenge of step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that איסר means attaching to a שבועה

steps.title: איסר 'with a שבועה' shows attaching
steps.stepSummary: The source is 'או אסרה איסר על נפשה בשבועה'. The איסר is made 'with' a שבועה, so it rests on an existing שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Or she forbade an איסר on herself with a שבועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that describes איסר as being done 'בשבועה', with a שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'בשבועה' suggests the איסר leans on a שבועה that is already there. That fits אביי's idea of attaching.

keyTerms.meaning: She placed a prohibition on herself
With an oath (by means of a שבועה)

phrases.english: as it is written: "Or she bound a bond
upon herself with an oath"

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״אוֹ אָסְרָה אִסָּר עַל נַפְשָׁהּ בִּשְׁבֻעָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'בשבועה' shows the איסר is attached to a שבועה

steps.title: But מבטא is also written 'with a שבועה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that מבטא is also described as 'בשבועה', in 'לכל אשר יבטא האדם בשבועה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: מבטא too is written that way: 'Whatever a person will say clearly with a שבועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the proof from step 12, because the very same wording, 'בשבועה', is used for מבטא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'בשבועה' proves that איסר means attaching, then מבטא should also mean attaching, since it too is joined to 'בשבועה'. So the proof no longer separates the two words.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (brings a פסוק as a challenge)
Will say clearly

phrases.english: Mivta too:
but it is written: "Whatever a person will clearly utter
phrases.notes: ויקרא ה:ד, the same פסוק quoted in step 9

phrases.english: with an oath"!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְבַטֵּא נָמֵי – הָכְתִיב: ״לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יְבַטֵּא הָאָדָם בִּשְׁבֻעָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof given in step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof that 'בשבועה' shows איסר means attaching
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מבטא also appears with 'בשבועה', so by the same logic מבטא would mean attaching too

steps.title: אביי brings a new source that 'utterance' means an oath
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves that מבטא means שבועה from a פסוק that lists only נדרים and מבטא as the ways a woman binds herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: we learn that מבטא is a שבועה from here: 'And if she be married to a husband, while her vows are upon her, or the utterance of her lips with which she bound her soul.' The פסוק does not mention a שבועה. So with what did she bind herself, other than her vows? With מבטא. That means מבטא is the שבועה.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 13 pointed out that the old source for מבטא (ויקרא ה:ד, from step 9) also says 'בשבועה', which would spoil the proof for איסר. אביי answers by bringing a different פסוק to prove that מבטא means a שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק lists only two ways a woman binds herself: her נדרים and the מבטא of her lips. The word שבועה never appears, yet a woman can certainly make a שבועה. So the שבועה must be hiding in the word מבטא.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'utterance', a clear spoken statement; here shown to mean a שבועה
From here; it introduces a source
She bound her soul, meaning she forbade something to herself
With what?

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
phrases.notes: 'Rather' means he drops the old source for מבטא from step 9, since that פסוק also says 'בשבועה'. The proof for איסר in step 12 stays.

phrases.english: That 'utterance' means an oath, we learn from here:
"And if she be married to a husband,
while her vows are upon her,
or the utterance of her lips,
with which she has bound her soul" —
while it does not mention an oath;
With what did she bind herself? With 'utterance.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: מִבְטָא שְׁבוּעָה מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13. It replaces the step 9 source for מבטא (ויקרא ה:ד, which also says 'בשבועה') with במדבר 30:7, so the 'בשבועה' proof for איסר in step 12 still stands.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר 30:7 mentions only vows and מבטא, so מבטא must be the שבועה

steps.title: רבא reads the teaching differently: 'bond' can also be an oath
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that attaching to a שבועה is not a real שבועה. So he explains the ברייתא this way: מבטא is a שבועה, and איסר can also be a שבועה. It depends on whether it was said in the language of a נדר or of a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Really, I will tell you that attaching to a שבועה is not like saying a שבועה with your own mouth. This is what the ברייתא means: מבטא is a שבועה. איסר is also a שבועה. The פסוק placed איסר between נדר and שבועה. If a person said it in the language of a נדר, it is a נדר. If he said it in the language of a שבועה, it is a שבועה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a different way to read the ברייתא, one that does not need איסר to mean 'attaching to a שבועה' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי needed איסר to mean מתפיס because he holds that attaching counts as a שבועה. רבא disagrees: in his view, attaching is not a שבועה, so the ברייתא could not be calling it one. He explains that איסר is a middle word. The language the person used decides whether it is a נדר or a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I will tell you; it keeps an earlier position and explains it differently
Attaching something to an existing שבועה, saying 'this should be like that'
Like saying a שבועה out loud with one's own mouth
The פסוק placed it
The wording of a vow or the wording of an oath

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of promise. A נדר forbids an object ('this bread is forbidden to me'). A שבועה binds the person ('I swear I won't eat'). רבא says an איסר can go either way, depending on the wording used.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the two אמוראים read the same ברייתא differently because of a deeper disagreement about מתפיס בשבועה. Step 18 makes that disagreement explicit.

phrases.english: Rava said: Actually, I will tell you,
that attaching to an oath
is not like expressing an oath from one's own mouth;
and this is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the ברייתא the גמרא has been working through, which explains the words מבטא and איסר.

phrases.english: "Utterance" is an oath.
"Bond" is also an oath.
The prohibition of a 'bond' —
the verse placed it between a vow and an oath;
if he expressed it in the language of a vow, it is a vow;
in the language of an oath, it is an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading from אביי's, one that rejects the idea that איסר means attaching to a שבועה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says איסר is a שבועה and then seems to doubt it ('אם אתה אומר...'). אביי solved this by reading איסר as מתפיס, but רבא holds that מתפיס is not a שבועה.
steps.terutzMaskana: איסר can be either a נדר or a שבועה, depending on the wording used; attaching is not a real שבועה

steps.title: Where does the verse put 'bond' between vow and oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק places איסר between נדר and שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where did the פסוק place it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבא's claim. It is setting up the next step, which will quote the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said that איסר sits between נדר and שבועה. The גמרא now wants to see exactly which פסוק shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: Where?

phrases.english: Where did it place it?
phrases.notes: He means: where did the פסוק put the word איסר between vow and oath?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבא's claim
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that places איסר between נדר and שבועה

steps.title: The verse: vowed, or bound a bond, with an oath
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק reads 'נדרה, or אסרה איסר, בשבועה.' The word איסר sits right between נדרה and בשבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And if she vowed in her husband's house, or bound her soul with a bond, with an oath.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting the פסוק where איסר sits between נדר and שבועה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order of the words is the proof. נדרה comes first, then אסרה איסר, then בשבועה. Since איסר is in the middle, it can lean toward either side, a נדר or a שבועה.

keyTerms.meaning: She vowed
A 'bond', a self-imposed prohibition

phrases.english: "And if she vowed in her husband's house,
or bound her soul with a bond
with an oath, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: במדבר 30:11, where איסר appears between נדרה and בשבועה

steps.title: אביי and רבא follow their known dispute about attaching to an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי and רבא are each consistent with their own view in the well-known מחלוקת about מתפיס בשבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they each follow their own reasoning. For it was stated: about one who attaches to a שבועה, אביי said it is like saying a שבועה with one's own mouth, and רבא said it is not like saying a שבועה with one's own mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up by showing that the two readings of the ברייתא come from a disagreement אביי and רבא already have elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that attaching counts as a שבועה, so he could read איסר as מתפיס and needed a separate source for מבטא. רבא holds that attaching does not count, so he had to read איסר as a real נדר or שבועה. Each reading fits its author's known position.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning; each one is consistent with his known view
One who attaches something to an existing prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: אביי: attaching to a שבועה counts like a שבועה, so איסר in the ברייתא means מתפיס and מבטא is learned from במדבר 30:7. רבא: attaching does not count, so איסר is a middle word that becomes a נדר or a שבועה based on the wording used.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning;
as it was stated: one who attaches to an oath —

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: כְּמוֹצִיא שְׁבוּעָה מִפִּיו דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: Abaye said: it is like expressing an oath from his mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְרָבָא אָמַר: לָאו כְּמוֹצִיא שְׁבוּעָה מִפִּיו דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: and Rava said: it is not like expressing an oath from his mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the two readings of אביי and רבא to their broader known dispute
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The two readings of the ברייתא come from the מחלוקת over whether מתפיס בשבועה counts as a real שבועה

steps.title: A ברייתא defines איסר as attaching to an existing vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: the Torah's איסר is someone who forbids meat and wine on himself 'like the day my father died' and similar days. שמואל says this works only if he has been under a vow from that day on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא objects from a ברייתא: What is the איסר mentioned in the Torah? It is a person who says, 'It is upon me that I will not eat meat and will not drink wine, like the day my father died,' or 'like the day so-and-so died,' or 'like the day גדליה בן אחיקם was killed,' or 'like the day I saw ירושלים destroyed.' He is forbidden. And שמואל said: this is only when he has been under a vow from that day on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא and a comment of שמואל to set up a challenge. The actual question comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a real example of the Torah's איסר. שמואל explains that the person already had a vow against meat and wine on that day, and now he is linking a new vow to it. So the ברייתא's איסר turns out to be a case of attaching to an existing vow.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'binding' that a person puts on himself, mentioned in the Torah
'It is upon me.' The standard way to take on a vow
Has been under a vow from then until now
The governor whose killing is mourned on צום גדליה

steps.confusionAlert: The days in the ברייתא are not just sad days. שמואל explains that the person must have actually vowed on that day. That is why this counts as attaching to an earlier vow, not just a comparison.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
What is the 'איסר' mentioned in the Torah?
One who says: 'It is upon me that I will not eat meat
and that I will not drink wine'
like the day on which his father died,
phrases.notes: Literally 'his father,' but it means the speaker's own father.

phrases.english: like the day on which so-and-so died,

phrases.aramaic: כְּיוֹם שֶׁנֶּהֱרַג בּוֹ גְּדַלְיָה בֶּן אֲחִיקָם,
phrases.english: like the day on which Gedaliah ben Ahikam was killed,
like the day he saw Jerusalem in its destruction, he is forbidden.
And Shmuel said:
And that is only when he has been under a vow from that day on.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an outside source about the meaning of איסר to test the two explanations of אביי and רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that איסר is simply a plain נדר or שבועה, depending on the wording
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With שמואל's explanation, the ברייתא's example of איסר is a case of attaching (מתפיס) to an earlier vow. That fits a view that treats איסר as attaching.

steps.title: The ברייתא fits אביי's view
steps.stepSummary: For אביי this works well. Attaching to a נדר makes a נדר, so attaching to a שבועה makes a שבועה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works well for אביי: since attaching to a נדר makes a נדר, attaching to a שבועה makes a שבועה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא fits אביי without any trouble. This sets up the coming question against רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא with שמואל proves that attaching to a vow really works. אביי reasons that the same is true for a שבועה, so מתפיס בשבועה is a real שבועה, which is his view. The 'בשלמא' (granted) wording tells us a 'but for רבא...' is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Granted.' It works for one side, and a problem for the other side follows.
Attaching or linking a new statement to an existing vow or oath

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core of the well-known מחלוקת about מתפיס בשבועה. If attaching works for a נדר, can it also work for a שבועה?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Abaye,
since one who attaches to a vow makes a vow,
one who attaches to an oath makes an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא for אביי's side as the first half of a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא, who holds that attaching to a שבועה is not a real שבועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the Torah's איסר is a case of attaching, and the פסוק places איסר next to שבועה, it points to attaching working for a שבועה too. That fits אביי and seems hard for רבא.
